questions_and_answers.question: What does Part D explain about clauses consisting only of adjectives and adverbs?

answers.answer: They should be translated as passive sentences
They can be translated using a relative clause with ‘to be’

questions_and_answers.question: Which city is mentioned in the first example of Part D?
In example 1, what is the Czech Question concerned with?

answers.answer: How to reduce a post‑war creation without unleashing a European war

questions_and_answers.question: Which minister destroyed the entire air force according to the notes of von Bülow‑Schwante?
In the secret command instruction, what will conclude the period of tension preceding war?
What is the principal subject of the Vienna report by Papen?

answers.answer: The British and French Prime Ministers

questions_and_answers.question: Which German word in example 2 is translated as ‘air force’?
What warning does the section provide about adjectives and adverbs?

answers.answer: They cannot be distinguished in German
The same word may function as an adjective or an adverb depending on its use
Adverbs always take a special ending
Adjectives never appear in extended constructions

questions_and_answers.question: Which example is associated with Mussolini’s Berlin visit?
What does the word ‘möglichst’ indicate in example 3?

answers.answer: It is an adjective meaning possible
It is an adverb meaning as … as possible
It is a noun meaning possibility
It is a verb meaning to be able

articles.text:
Part D explains that a clause consisting of adjectives and adverbs alone can be translated by forming a relative clause with the verb “to be.”

Example 1 vocabulary:
Der Reichskanzler,- (Chancellor)
Die Bilanz,-en (balance)
Der Ausblick (outlook)
Betrachten (to regard)
Die Unterhaltung,-en (conversation)
Der Gesichtspunkt,-e (standpoint)
Das Nachkriegsgebilde,- (post‑war creation)
Die Entfesselung (unleashing)
Die Entwicklung,-en (development)
Reduzieren (to reduce)

Example 1 sentence:
Der Deutsche Botschafter in Wien an den Führer und Reichskanzler. Inhalt: Bilanz 1936 und Ausblick. Wien, den 12. Januar 1937. A.A. eing. 15. Januar 1937 Nm. (Pol IV 229). In Warschau betrachtet man, wie ich aus vielen Unterhaltungen mit meinen hiesigen Kollegen feststellen konnte, die tschechische Frage nur unter dem Gesichtspunkt, wie man dieses Nachkriegsgebilde ohne die Entfesselung eines europäischen Krieges auf einen für die mitteleuropäische Entwicklung möglichen Zustand reduzieren könnte. Papen.

Translation:
The German Ambassador in Vienna to the Führer and Chancellor. Vienna, January 12, 1937. Foreign Office, arrived January 15, 1937 PM (Pol IV 229). Subject: Balance for 1936 and outlook. In Warsaw, as I was able to ascertain from many conversations with my colleagues, the Czech Question is regarded only from the standpoint of how one could reduce this post‑war creation to a state possible for Central European development without unleashing a European war. – Papen.

Example 2 vocabulary:
Der Aufenthalt (visit)
Pazifistisch (pacifistic)
Eingestellt (oriented)
Die Luftwaffe (air force)
Zerschlagen (to destroy, smash)
Die Machtübernahme (assumption of power)
Befindlich (to be)
Übernehmen (to receive, take over)

Example 2 text:
Aufzeichnung des Gesandten von Bülow‑Schwante, Auswärtiges Amt (Unterhaltung während des Berliner Aufenthalts Mussolinis). Der pazifistisch eingestellte Ministerpräsident Nitti habe die ganze Luftwaffe zerschlagen, und bei seiner Machtübernahme hätte er nur einige hundert in schlechtem Zustand befindliche Flugzeuge übernommen …

Translation:
Notes of Minister von Bülow‑Schwante, Foreign Office (Conversation during Mussolini’s Berlin visit). The pacifistically oriented Minister President Nitti destroyed the entire air force, and at the time of his assumption of power he had received only several hundred airplanes in bad condition…

Example 3 vocabulary:
Die Kommandosache,-n (Command Business)
Der Chef,-s (Commander, Chief)
Der Offizier,-e (officer)
Der Entwurf,-e (draft)
Die Weisung,-en (instruction)
Vorausgehen (to precede)
Die Spannungszeit (period of tension)
Plötzlich (sudden)
Der Zeitpunkt (time)
Der Umfang (extent)
Überraschen (to surprise)
Militärisch (military)
Das Handeln (action)
Unsererseits (by our side)
Der Abschluss (conclusion)

Example 3 text:
Geheime Kommandosache. Chef Sache. Nur durch Offizier. Von Offizier geschrieben. Berlin, den 20. Mai 1938. Entwurf für die neue Weisung “Grün”. Aber auch eine solche, dem Krieg vorausgehende Spannungszeit wird durch plötz­liches, dem Zeitpunkt und dem Umfang nach möglichst überraschendes militärisches Handeln unsererseits ihren Abschluss finden.

Translation:
Secret Command Business. For the Commander only. Transmitted by officer only. Written by officer. Berlin, May 20, 1938. Draft for the new instruction “Green.” But also such a period of tension preceding the war will be concluded by sudden military action by our side with the greatest possible surprise as regards the time and extent.

This section cautions that the same word may be an adjective or an adverb depending on its use. In example 1, *möglichen* is an adjective, while in example 3, *möglichst* (the superlative) is an adverb.
